experiment.answers: the gap the composition receipt recorded against the forge -- 'a single-primitive check reuses the same launch it is supposed to be testing'

headline: The composition block recorded a GAP IN THE GATE rather than only a fixed bug: the forge verifies every candidate through the op's OWN execute(), so it never varies the LAUNCH, which is how the tiled matmul stayed wrong at every m not a multiple of the tile while every check passed. This is the sweep that would have caught it -- and the first version of the sweep REPORTED ZERO FAILURES FOR FOUR PRIMITIVES IT NEVER RAN.

MY_OWN_FUZZ_COULD_NOT_FAIL_FOR_FOUR_PRIM.what_happened: round one printed 0 wrong over 2322 shapes. matmul_simdgroup, attention, top-k and sparse recorded ZERO CASES -- the simdgroup filter demanded every dimension be a multiple of 8 and the awkward grid held exactly ONE such value, and the other three were simply never written.
MY_OWN_FUZZ_COULD_NOT_FAIL_FOR_FOUR_PRIM.how_it_was_caught: by asking which primitives APPEAR in the per-primitive table, not by reading the loop. A missing key is visible; a zero count inside a passing summary is not.
MY_OWN_FUZZ_COULD_NOT_FAIL_FOR_FOUR_PRIM.why_it_is_the_same_class: this program has sealed the check-that-cannot-fail four times -- a gate blind to magnitude, a predicate that accepted an all-zeros pack, a tie-break mutation on dead code, and a curve counting the absence of probed blockers. Here it is in the instrument built to find it.
MY_OWN_FUZZ_COULD_NOT_FAIL_FOR_FOUR_PRIM.shipped: kernel_forge.shape_sweep RAISES on zero cases. A sweep that executed nothing cannot report zero failures, and the message says to check the shape FILTER rather than the kernel.

the_sweep_itself.shapes_include: 1, primes, one above and one below a threadgroup multiple, very wide, very narrow, and for the simdgroup strategy nine multiples of 8 including non-multiples of 16

prediction_refuted.written: at least ONE more primitive is wrong at some awkward shape, because this program has found the same class three times
prediction_refuted.measured: 2885 shapes across 15 primitive/strategy combinations, ZERO wrong and ZERO raised
prediction_refuted.verdict: REFUTED, and it is the good kind of refutation: after the launch fix the primitives are shape-robust across every awkward shape tried. The prediction was reasonable and the answer is better than it expected.
prediction_refuted.what_it_does_not_prove: absence of shape-dependent defects, only that 2885 specific shapes are correct. The tiled matmul's bug lived at m % tile != 0, a condition this grid hits constantly -- a defect keyed on something the grid does not vary, dtype or threadgroup width, would still be invisible.

shipped.kernel_forge.shape_sweep: varies the shape, records a RAISE as a FAILURE rather than a skip, refuses a zero-case sweep
shipped.kernel_forge.AWKWARD_SHAPES: the grid, so a caller does not reinvent a filter that silently excludes everything
shipped.pinned_by_test: a one-shape check PASSES the tiled matmul's defect and the sweep does not -- the regression is expressed as the difference between the two, which is the whole point of the gap

claim_boundary.one_dtype: f32 throughout; the sweep varies SHAPE and nothing else
claim_boundary.one_threadgroup_width: every primitive runs at its default; the top-k receipt already showed a race that only fires at 1024, so width is a SECOND axis this sweep does not cover
claim_boundary.not_wired_into_the_forge_loop: shape_sweep is available and tested; forge() still verifies one shape per candidate, because the forge tunes an ELEMENTWISE chain where the launch is a 1-D grid over n and the shape axis is degenerate. Wiring it where it would be decoration is not a fix.
claim_boundary.nothing_timed: correctness only; no performance claim moves
